P2 synthesis — defend the architecture choice for this case: A design reviewer is evaluating this scenario: A team tells Claude Code “never touch production,” but every developer environment has production admin credentials. What is strongest? Which recommendation should they defend?

Remove/restrict production credentials and permissions; keep the instruction as supplemental guidance. Hard permission boundaries should not depend on model compliance. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.

P2 edge-case review — what action should survive scrutiny here? Apply the approved team-level Claude tools and environments guidance to this case: Each developer has a different MCP/tool configuration and shared workflows behave inconsistently. What should the team do?

Standardize high-value repository/team configuration and version it. Shared configuration improves reproducibility and governance. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.

P2 synthesis — defend the architecture choice for this case: A design reviewer is evaluating this scenario: An agent writes a large refactor and tests pass, but nobody reviews whether the tests cover the risk. What is missing? Which recommendation should they defend?

Independent human/system verification of both the change and test adequacy. Passing tests are evidence, not a substitute for judging whether verification is sufficient. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.

P2 edge-case review — what action should survive scrutiny here? Apply the approved AI-assisted developer workflows guidance to this case: A developer asks an agent to “make it work” using production admin credentials. What is the strongest correction?

Use a scoped development/test environment and require approval for shared/destructive actions. Developer productivity should not expand unnecessary production capability. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.

P2 synthesis — defend the architecture choice for this case: A design reviewer is evaluating this scenario: Quality drops after a deployment. Which evidence should be checked first? Which recommendation should they defend?

Model/prompt versions, retrieval/index changes, traces, and input-distribution changes around the deployment. Debugging starts from correlated evidence around the affected layer/change. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.

P2 edge-case review — what action should survive scrutiny here? Apply the approved debugging and operational issue resolution guidance to this case: An agent suddenly receives “permission denied” from a tool. What areas are most relevant?

Credentials, scopes, authorization policy, tool contract, and dependency status. Tool failures should be diagnosed at the integration/permission boundary. This P1 variant tests the same approved principle in a re-framed design review.
